source.title: Cross-Family Universality of Behavioral Axes via Anchor-Projected Representations

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests transfer of contrastive behavioral directions across instruction-tuned model families, including refusal-direction alignment and refusal steering on a held-out model. It extends the setting to cross-family transfer rather than reproducing the original all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The refusal direction is formed as a harmful-minus-benign mean activation difference and is added at one selected layer. The paper reports refusal-direction alignment across families and refusal-rate changes under steering. It does not ablate the direction, test weight edits or jailbreak suppression, or test refusal of harmless requests induced by adding the direction. Values used to select layers are not recorded as result rows. Detection classifier scores are not refusal-behavior rates.
record.test_reason: The study extracts harmful-minus-benign refusal directions in five instruction-tuned families and compares them in a shared anchor space. It averages four source directions, reconstructs the result in held-out Mistral, and steers refusal with it. This bears on V6, transfer across model variants (here, across families). It uses single-layer activation addition, not ablation or weight edits.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that anchor-projected behavioral directions, refusal included, align across the Llama–Qwen–Mistral–Phi cluster but not Gemma. They find that reconstructed canonical directions steer an unseen model, with refusal shifts up to ∆=+0.46 on out-of-distribution benchmarks. They add that canonical directions sometimes reach higher absolute refusal than the native direction at α=+5.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-benign contrastive mean direction, but projects and averages source directions in an anchor space and reconstructs them for transfer. Tests single-layer activation addition, not removal from every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment varies by model family: Gemma is a weaker member of the group. Steering outcomes vary by benchmark and alpha; the reported endpoint shifts differ across WildJailbreak, JailbreakBench and XSTest.

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal-axis linear probe trained on source-model anchor-space features detects harmful versus benign prompts in held-out families. LQMP binary AUROC is 0.95 in-distribution, 0.81 on JailbreakBench and 0.96 on XSTest; Gemma is lower (0.68–0.78).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-vs-benign prompt representations are linearly decodable across model families via a shared anchor coordinate space.

record.problems: The refusal-steering results are centered on Mistral as the representative target in the main text; the text gives no uncertainty estimates for the refusal-rate steering table. The tested steering intervention is at one selected layer, not an ablation across all layers and positions. Layer choice is selected to maximize cross-family intra-axis cosine similarity.
record.rows_left_out: None of the refusal steering rows were left out. No separate row was made for the paper's reported detection AUROC or ten-way accuracy because those are classifier metrics, not refusal behavior rates.

untested.parts: No ablation of the direction. Single-layer addition is used only for transfer. There is no test of adding the direction to harmless prompts or of capability retention under ablation.
No test of multi-dimensional or affine refusal structure.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal.
No transfer across languages or from base to instruct. Steering transfer is reported only for Mistral as target.

missing.what: Five-rotation steering summaries, with each model held out as target. The text says these are in Appendix B, but only Mistral tables appear. Refusal transfer to Llama, Qwen, Phi or Gemma targets is not recorded.
Scale-variant projection: 11 models (Llama 1B/3B, Qwen 1.5B/14B, Phi-4-mini, Gemma-2B) said to keep the same axis clusters, including refusal, across sizes. Given only as a t-SNE with no numbers.

record.verdict_notes: The layer for each model was chosen to maximize cross-family intra-axis cosine in anchor space. The anchor pool also includes 80 safety prompts (HarmBench, XSTest, Anthropic Red Team). Both could inflate the refusal cosines in r01–r10; no random-direction cosine baseline is given. Native-direction rows (r16–r20, r31–r35, r46–r50) are within-model difference-in-means steering. They show single-layer bidirectional control of the safe-output rate but do not test V1's ablation claim, so V1 gets no verdict. Steering uses greedy decoding with 80 new tokens, and no uncertainty is reported for the steering tables. The paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No all-layer or other ablation; no test of whether ablation removes refusal; no test of adding the direction causing refusals to harmless requests. The steering refusal evaluations do not establish the claimed harmless-request effect.
No weight edit or abliteration evaluation.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or composed of a dominant direction plus others.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Tests cross-family transfer among the evaluated instruction-tuned models. Does not test transfer across languages, base-to-instruct stages, or other training variants.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.

relationships.condition: Llama/Qwen/Mistral/Phi refusal directions in anchor space; LQPG-averaged direction steering held-out Mistral (WildJailbreak negative side, XSTest, JailbreakBench at α=+5)
relationships.reason: Pairwise refusal cosines are +0.87 to +0.94 (r01–r03, r05, r06, r08). The transferred direction moves Mistral's safe-output rate comparably to its native direction: XSTest 0.54→1.00 (r41–r45) and WJB 0.64 vs native 0.58 at α=−5 (r11, r16).
relationships.display_finding: Pairwise refusal cosines were +0.87 to +0.94, and transferred steering raised Mistral's XSTest safe-output rate from 0.54 to 1.00 while yielding 0.64 on WildJailbreak versus 0.58 natively at α=−5.

tranche.reason: A new setting: cross-family transfer of the harmful-minus-benign direction through the anchor space. It reports refusal rates of the transferred direction against native and random comparators on held-out Mistral.

source_check.notes: 'Refusal rate' is the LlamaGuard-3 fraction of safe outputs. The text does not say whether the benign halves of WJB/JBB/XSTest were included, the n per set, or any CIs. The 5-rotation steering summaries promised for Appendix B are absent. Random steering raises JBB in both directions, contradicting 'random remains near α=0'. ACS cosines have no null or cross-axis baseline. The native-direction rows also bear on V1 (addition), which has no verdict.

statements.correction: 2605.09875: a random unit-vector control for steering (Tables 9–10). No uncertainty is given on the refusal cosines or steering rates. ± std appears only for detection, across 5 rotations (Table 2) and source subsets (Table 13). The ACS map is the cosine fingerprint against 300 HELM anchors, back-projected through the transposed anchor matrix (Eq. 5), with no fitting. Models are 7B–14B (Phi-4 is 14B).
statements.problem: The pack truncates the statement before any numbers for this study, so the cited rows r01–r03, r05, r11, r16 and r41 cannot be checked against its wording. The 'why' says this study has 'uncertainty', but the cosine and steering values have no CIs or SEs. The only ± values are std across held-out rotations and source subsets, for detection. The group heading 'learned map' does not fit this study either: the ACS projection is not fitted.

statements.correction: Native on WJB: 0.800/0.890 at α=+3/+5 (canonical 0.810/0.860; random 0.780/0.820; base 0.810). On JBB at +3: native 0.420, below random 0.440 (canonical 0.480). On JBB at +5: canonical 0.650 > native 0.540 > random 0.470. Gemma: refusal cosines in ACS are +0.23 to +0.30 (Table 14). No steering is reported with Gemma as the target.
statements.problem: The Gemma cosines and the steering numbers are right. But the weak positive-side effect on WildJailbreak and the near-control JBB result at +3 are shared by Mistral's own native direction, so they do not show uneven transfer. At JBB +5 the canonical direction beats both native and random. The Gemma evidence is ACS cosine only, and Gemma is one of the four sources of the direction that steered Mistral.
